message.content: {"findings": [{"cwe": "CWE-22", "class": "Unpacker", "method": "process", "explanation": "The method uses the ZIP entry name after mapper.map() as a relative child path in new File(outputDir, name) without verifying that the resolved path remains under outputDir. A malicious ZIP entry such as '../../evil.txt' or an absolute path can therefore be written outside the intended extraction directory, allowing arbitrary file creation or overwrite."}, {"cwe": "CWE-22", "class": "BackslashUnpacker", "method": "process", "explanation": "The method splits backslash-separated ZIP entry names into path segments and constructs File objects from each segment without rejecting '..' or absolute segments. An entry such as '..\\..\\evil.txt' makes parentDirectory traverse outside outputDir, so FileUtils.copy can write to an arbitrary location."}, {"cwe": "CWE-22", "class": "Unwraper", "method": "process", "explanation": "The method creates the extraction target by applying mapper.map() to the entry name with only the detected root prefix removed, but it does not validate that the resulting path remains within outputDir. A crafted ZIP entry containing '../' after the root can escape the intended directory and overwrite files outside it."}]}
